title: A 1963 computer let its user draw directly on screen
body: Ivan Sutherland's Sketchpad ran on the TX-2 computer. A light pen let a designer indicate points on the display, and the program could apply geometric constraints while the designer moved parts of a drawing.
takeaway: A computer drawing can store relationships between shapes as well as the positions of their lines.
source: Ivan Sutherland, Sketchpad, MIT doctoral thesis (1963)
visual: a light pen touching a simple geometric outline on an early computer display

title: The original Game Boy played cartridges on a 7 cm screen
body: Nintendo introduced the Game Boy in 1989. It played interchangeable game cartridges on a monochrome display about 7.4 cm across the diagonal, small enough to fit into a portable handheld machine.
takeaway: Separating the cartridge from the handheld let one small machine become many games.
source: Computer History Museum, Timeline of Computer History (1989)
visual: an unbranded vintage handheld game device with a blank display and a cartridge beside it
